These seven columns all have null_rate 0.0 and are proposed as required; together they plausibly identify one scheduled flight departure since carrier+flight+origin+scheduled time distinguishes same-numbered flights on a given date, while tailnum (0.9% null) and actual times (2.9-3.3% null) cannot serve as grain keys.

dep_time (null_rate 0.029388), dep_delay (0.029388), arr_time (0.0307), air_time (0.032981), and arr_delay (0.032981) share comparable null rates consistent with the operator context that a flight which never departed has no departure time, so nulls are retained rather than imputed or dropped.
tailnum has null_rate 0.009154 (1521 of 166158 rows); the column is kept nullable rather than imputed since a missing tail number is a legitimate capture gap, not an error.

purpose: This table holds one row per scheduled flight departure from the three New York City airports (EWR, JFK, LGA) for January through June 2013, as reported by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics via the nycflights13 source, feeding downstream analysis of flight volume, delays, and carrier performance.
usage: Join on carrier and tailnum for aircraft-level analysis, or on time_hour for hourly weather joins as in the broader nycflights13 ecosystem; dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, arr_delay, and air_time are null for flights that never departed or arrived, so consumers computing delay statistics must explicitly filter or account for these nulls rather than treating them as zero.
limitations: Cleanup could not resolve the 2.9%-3.3% null rates on dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, arr_delay, and air_time, which represent cancelled or otherwise incomplete flights rather than data quality defects; tailnum is missing for 0.9% of rows; the dataset itself is scoped to only the first six months of 2013 and only the three NYC origin airports, so it is not a complete annual or national flight record.
